s: to hand over something to someone, entrust someone with something, confer a right on someone
to be passed on to someone (of a disease or illness)
to communicate itself to someone (of enthusiasm, nervousness, etc.)
übertragen.et: From Middle High German übertragen, at least in part a calque of Latin transferre. Analysable as über- (“over”) + tragen (“to carry”). Compare Dutch overdragen, English carry over.

s: to exceed, to surpass, to outdo
Ich übertreibe nicht, er ist wirklich über 2 Meter groß.
I'm not exaggerating, he really is over two meters tall.
Übertreiben Sie Ihr Training am ersten Tag nicht.
Don't overdo your training on the first day.
Ich glaube, wir haben es gestern mit dem Alkohol etwas übertrieben.
I think we went a bit overboard with the alcohol yesterday.
übertreiben.et: Inherited from Middle High German übertrīben, equivalent to über- + treiben

s: carrier (person or animal transmitting a disease without contracting it)
transgression, trespass, breach, violation, infringement, prevarication
to join (another faith, party, etc.); to convert to [with zu]
to enter, to pass into (a different medium, phase of life, etc.) [with von (+ dative) ‘from’] [with in (+ accusative) ‘into’]
to step beyond (a line in the long jump) with one's foot
to overflow its banks (of a river)
übertreten.et: From Middle High German übertreten. By surface analysis, über (“over”) + treten (“to step”).

s: to step beyond; to trespass; to violate; to breach
Ich würde meine Grenzen nicht übertreten wollen.
I just wouldn't want to overstep my boundaries.
to whitewash (to paint (a building, a wall, etc.) a bright white with whitewash)
übertünchen.et: From über- + tünchen (inseparable) or über + tünchen (separable).
